To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the serum albumin-water distribution of ionogenic organic compounds (IOCs) depends on the three-dimensional structure and the position of the substituents, and that the serum albumic-water partition coefficients (log KBSA/w) of IOCs cannot be reliably predicted from their physicochemical properties or from the serum albumin-octanol partition coefficients.

the binding of organic anions to bovine serum albumine (BSA) is strongly influenced by the three dimensional structure and position of substitutions on sorbing molecules, and that conventional modeling approaches (e. g. based on octanol water partition coefficients) poorly describe the binding of organic ions to BSA.
the partition coefficients of structurally diverse anionic and cationic organic ions to bovine serum albumins are substantially influenced by the structure of the chemical.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the partitioning of organic ions to the major blood plasma protein, bovine serum albu- min, and its influence on the freely dissolved concentration and the bioaccumulation of these chemicals in the human body.
the development of a new approach to assess the bioaccumulation and the toxicity of organic chemicals.
the partitioning of structurally diverse organic ions to the major protein in the blood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the serum albumin-water distribution coefficient (KBSA) of a chemical depends on the chemical's structure and its position of substitutions.
the serum albumin-water distribution of organic ions is strongly affected by the three-dimensional chemical structure of the sorbing molecules, which has to be considered in future modeling efforts.
the binding of organic ions to bovine serum albumins is strongly influenced by their chemical structure and the position of the substituents on the molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the partitioning of organic ions to serum albumin depends on the three-dimensional structure and the charge distribution of the sorbing molecule.
the binding of organic ions to serum albumin is strongly influenced by the three-dimensionsal structure of the chemicals, and that conventional modeling approaches poorly capture these effects.
partitioning of organic anions to BSA is a complex and poorly understood process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partitioning of ionogenic chemicals to bovine serum album in is strongly influenced by steric effects, which are not captured in current partitioning models.

the binding behavior of organic ions to serum albumin is strongly affected by the three-dimensional shape of the chemicals and that partition coefficients for organic ions can be predicted only by using a model that takes the steric effects into account.
serum albumin-water distribution of organic ions is a complex process that is not well understood.
